title: Component Count

story.briefing: The same question as the floor plan, asked of the network itself. How many separate pieces did the outage leave behind?
story.success: Fragments counted. The scale of the break is finally known.

description: A graph is given as n, the number of nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and edges, an array of [u, v] pairs. Edges are undirected unless stated otherwise, and there are no self-loops or duplicate edges. Return the number of connected pieces the graph falls into. A node with no edges is a piece of its own.

examples.explanation: Every isolated node is its own piece.

hints: This is the grid problem again with different scenery: start from an unvisited node, mark everything connected to it, and that is one piece.
Do not restart the search from every node. A node already marked belongs to a piece you have counted, and searching from it again is wasted work.
Build a neighbour list and a visited array. Loop over every node; when you find an unvisited one, add one to the count and walk its whole component, marking as you go.
